cells.tense: You are giving and receiving on fair terms right now, and you know it.
cells.ask: Name one finished thing you're still watching and set down the watching. Leave it released for a day.
cells.core:
When something is finished, you put it down, and it stays down. You don't check on it an hour later or pick it up to see if it can be reworked. That clear give-and-take is rarer than it looks, and it reads like something you decided once and kept deciding.

What's still moving is quieter than the exchange. Some part of you stands over a released thing, watching what it does next, and that watching is the only loose end. Notice which put-down things you're still keeping an eye on. That's where the release hasn't counted yet. The trade on the table is already fair. It doesn't need a guard on it.
cells.sheetLine: You know when a thing is done and you put it down.
cells.verb: giving and receiving in fair exchange
cells.place: at an open door you've stopped gripping — what goes out stays out

cells.tense: You will be bracing for an imbalance that hasn't happened, and you're already guarding against it.
cells.ask: Take one exchange you're tracking and leave its ledger alone for a day. Let it sit however it sits.
cells.core:
You're running the math on whether they gave as much, whether you got back what you put in, and the math is ahead of the facts. You're auditing a trade that hasn't had time to be a trade yet.

Pressing it even costs you the exchange itself. Every gift arrives with a question attached — enough? matched? what it should be? Holding the exchange without pressing it looks different: you let the balance tip and stay tipped, you receive without reaching for the receipt. Let one thing sit uneven and see if anything actually breaks. The fairness you're protecting survives a day without the guard.

cells.tense: You stopped giving and receiving in fair exchange a while back, and you're still back there.
cells.ask: Make one exchange without tracking it. Give something and let it leave, or receive something and let it land without giving back right away.
cells.core:
You're behind a door that closed, giving and receiving from the far side of a moment you haven't walked past. Trades feel like risks you can't take, so you've stopped putting anything on the table that could come back changed.

What isn't moving is the plain ability to tell an even offer from an uneven one. That hasn't gone anywhere. It's willing, just not steering. One small exchange with no ledger attached will show you the difference between a trade you can take and one you can't. You don't have to trust every exchange. You only have to try one.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped trading fairly when something tilted, and you stayed stopped.

cells.tense: You are already releasing what no longer serves, but you're calling it something else — and the fairness runs without you owning it.
cells.ask: Name one thing you let go of this year and say out loud that you're the one who let it go.
cells.core:
Things end for you without ceremony. You stop returning to what's finished, and you don't keep old exchanges alive just to even them out. But you describe all of it as just what happened — the thing ended, the trade ran out, the season turned. You talk as though it occurred to you rather than as though you did it.

The fairness runs underneath that. You already give and receive on fair terms. You're simply not claiming it. The release happened; saying so is what makes it yours to keep. That's a small move, and it belongs to the person who made it.
cells.sheetLine: You release things already. You just don't take credit for it.
